params.body:
v0.29.0 carries the read token's `administration: read` (#89), so the VM has to move before
any of it reaches a measurement.

```
RELEASE     v0.28.1 -> v0.29.0
GATEWAY_SHA f46d8bb3… -> 45562a23…
```

The sha is `control-gateway-linux-amd64` from the release's `SHA256SUMS`, and the asset was
downloaded and hashed again before this was written: both read
`45562a231f6bdcb92801dfc79f47ecb54abe41e2df85d355e3eb86747ace54bd`. `bash -n` on the script
is clean.

After merge: `rehearse.sh upgrade`, then the cached read tokens on the box
(`elixir-app/storage/app/private/control/read-tokens/`) are the last thing in the way. They
live an hour and carry the rights of the moment they were minted, so until they expire or
are removed, protection keeps answering 403 on all 20 projects even with the new gateway
running. That hour is why this looked like a failed permission change earlier today.
params.title: De VM op v0.29.0
